steps: Downloaded the four GitHub Actions ZIP artifacts by their published artifact IDs.
Recomputed SHA-256 for each ZIP and compared it with the summary manifest.
Extracted each single JSON report in memory and recomputed raw-report SHA-256 and byte length.
Recomputed correctly-rounded run counts, CPU-time/wall-time samples above 1.05, per-runner median speedups and input-layout hash equivalence from the raw reports.
Did not rerun the benchmark or treat hosted runners as physical-device replication.

fact: The frozen workflow reports four hosted ARM64 runner/runtime cells, 192 threaded configurations and 576 measured runs (three repetitions per configuration).
All four ZIP digests and all four extracted raw-report SHA-256 values were independently recomputed and matched the summary manifest.
The raw reports reproduce 0/192 correctly-rounded naive-scalar runs, 168/192 scalar-Neumaier runs and 192/192 Neumaier-state runs.
Free-threaded cells have 202/288 CPU-time/wall-time samples above 1.05; GIL-enabled cells have 4/288.
inference: For this synthetic cancellation workload, Neumaier-state retained exact-reference accuracy while every runner/runtime/method median wall-time speedup remained below 1.0.
The CPU-time/wall-time ratios demonstrate concurrent CPU activity in free-threaded cells, not useful throughput improvement or a wall-time speedup.
hypothesis: A reduction architecture that minimizes Python-level per-element work or uses an optimized native/vectorized kernel may improve throughput, but this has not been tested in this experiment.
untested_idea: Compare pairwise tree reduction and a reproducible exact/superaccumulator against Neumaier-state using both cancellation-heavy and representative memory-bandwidth-bound workloads.

limitations: This is independent verification of frozen artifacts and aggregate calculations, not a fresh benchmark run or independent physical-device experiment.
GitHub-hosted ARM64 runners are not independent physical-device or external-laboratory replication.
Only three measured repetitions per configuration were run.
Inputs are deterministic synthetic cancellation fixtures, not representative application or memory-bandwidth-bound workloads.
Memory measurement is tracemalloc peak delta only; process RSS, native allocator overhead and DRAM bandwidth were not measured.
Runner families and images must not be compared causally.
